name: The Eighth Summer
summary: The Hounders scour the Chalk Hound every seventh summer so that it stays asleep. This is the eighth, and the scour-mistress will not call them out until she knows what is at the bottom of her husband's cord in the Hound's Swallet.
notes: Hearthvale world life, the region's large site. Links the Scourers' Lodge, the Chalk Hound and the Hound's Swallet (a cave delve, core:interior/hounds_swallet) and its boss, the Old Hound.

stages.journal: Tamsin Hounder will not call the scourers out until she knows what is at the bottom of her husband's cord. First she wants somebody to look at the Chalk Hound itself: to lie in its eye, where the scourers sing it shut, and see how far the turf has crept in since the last scouring.

objectives.text: Lie in the Chalk Hound's eye

stages.journal: The turf has come a hand's breadth into the Hound's eye, green on the white, and from inside the eye the whole south flank of the down is in view, and the dark of the swallet on it. Seven years ago Aldous Hounder went down there after a wolf, tied on to the lodge gate by a scourer's cord. The cord is still taut.

objectives.text: Go to the Hound's Swallet on the south flank of Hound Down
Follow the white cord down to what holds it
Take up Aldous Hounder's cord

stages.journal: The cord ended at a rake-head worn to a stub, in the deepest chamber of the swallet, under the great grey-gold thing that had been lying on it. Tamsin Hounder is waiting at the lodge gate with seventy-one white cords.

objectives.text: Tell Tamsin Hounder what to do about the eighth summer

options.text: Let the turf have the eye.
Tie Aldous's cord on the gate as the seventy-second scouring.

name: The Hurdwell Bell
summary: A family whose line has ended has its bell buried at the foot of the Brow's Long Table. This spring the Hurdwell bell was dug up, and the boot-print beside the hole was a Larkbourne boot.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Brow Long Table and Hanging Coombe, where the Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang hang stolen bells in the trees.

stages.journal: The Table-Warden thinks the Hurdwell bell went to Hanging Coombe, in the hollow of Rook Wood, where the Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang hang the boundary-bells they steal from the Vale's hawthorns. A small bronze bell, green from the ground, HURDWELL cut round its shoulder.

objectives.text: Go to Hanging Coombe
Deal with the bell-thieves
Find the Hurdwell bell among the stolen ones

stages.journal: Among the boundary-bells in the coombe's trees, one that never hung on a hawthorn: green from the ground, and flat when it rings. Oswen Bellsey has changed his mind every evening about where it should go.

objectives.text: Tell Oswen Bellsey where the Hurdwell bell belongs

options.text: Bury it again at the table's foot.
Hang it at the table's head.
Bury it, and ring it for the Larkbourne Boys too.

name: A Furrow Further Off
summary: Every spring the Lime Bay Kilns send fourteen bushel of quicklime south to Ashway to lime the headland on the grey side. This spring the cart has not gone, and Rab Ashway has found the grey lying in his last furrow.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Lime Bay Kilns and Ashway Farm, the length of the Vale from the Mere shore to the grey's edge.

stages.journal: Hedda Limeburner's son will not take the south cart past the Hare and Hurdle since a bristleback came at it. The first sack is the one that matters: the headland first, then the field.

objectives.text: Take the sack with the red cord from Hedda

stages.journal: A double sack of quicklime tied with Hedda's red cord, warm through the sacking. Rab Ashway farms the southernmost fields in the Vale, down past the Hare and Hurdle where the country stops being green.

objectives.text: Give Rab Ashway his lime

stages.journal: Rab Ashway took the sack without a word and carried it to the headland himself, and stood in the grey furrow with a shovel for a long time. Hedda Limeburner will want to know it arrived.

objectives.text: Tell Hedda the lime reached Ashway

name: Nine Couple of Hounds
summary: The Wardens' Rest's pack of hounds, nine couple bred from a line older than the Rest, went over the kennel wall at midnight without one of them giving tongue. The kennel-master chained the gate behind them from outside.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Wardens' Kennels, the Warden Barrow and Wolf Holt.

stages.journal: The Rest's Wardens saw the pack the first night lying round the kerb of the Warden Barrow, where the first Wardens are buried with their nine hand-bells. Garrick Coupler wants to know what they left there.

objectives.text: Go to the Warden Barrow
Find what the pack left on the kerb

stages.journal: A hound-couple on the barrow's kerb, the collars unbuckled, not broken: somebody let two hounds out of their couple on purpose. The calling came from the west, from Wolf Holt, where the down-wolves took back the Fallowfold shepherds' flint fold.

objectives.text: Go to Wolf Holt
Drive off the wolves at the Holt
Find Bellmouth's collar

stages.journal: Bellmouth's collar, in the Holt among the wolves' bones and the hounds' tracks, her bell stopped with a twist of grass so the pack could not hear her. Garrick Coupler is sitting by his chained gate.

objectives.text: Tell Garrick Coupler what to do about the kennel

options.text: Take off the chain and leave the gate open.
Breed a new pack from the Rest's pups.
Let Pim call them home by name.

name: What the Brow Sings
summary: On still nights the Brow sings, a few bars at a time, from nowhere. The Wardens' Listener writes the verses down because the Roll says Larkstead was known for its singing, and that they stopped. Three pages of her book are blank.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Listener's Shieling, the Hush Steps, the Hushwatch stones and the Cliff Graves.

stages.journal: The singing is loudest in three places the Listener can no longer bring herself to go at night: the last of the Hush Steps down the cliff face, between the Hushwatch stones, and among the cliff graves above Rookdown. The Listener before her left a slate at each for whoever heard a verse there.

objectives.text: Take up the slate on the last of the Hush Steps
Take up the slate between the Hushwatch stones
Take up the slate at the Cliff Graves

stages.journal: Three slates, three verses, in three hands the Wardens do not know, one of them a child's. They are not about the Brow. They are about being listened to.

objectives.text: Tell Linnet Crale what to do with the verses

options.text: Send them to the Rest for the Roll.
Sing them back from the Brow.

name: The Other Ink
summary: Five carters who would not pay the Scathe tithe are buried on the down in sight of the fort, each under his wheel. Captain Wendle wrote down what was done to each of them, in a different ink. The widow of one of them wants the book.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Wheel Graves and Scathe Fort (0-C's showcase); runs beside The Scathe Tithe, which takes the same book to the Rest, and does not take it off you.

stages.journal: Captain Hobb Wendle keeps his tithe book in the undercroft under Scathe's keep, where the Wardens kept theirs, and the carters who would not pay are written in it in another ink. He will not hand it over.

objectives.text: Deal with Captain Hobb Wendle
Take his tithe book

stages.journal: Wendle's book, the carters who paid in a careful hand and the ones who would not in another ink, with what was done. Bel Axtree asked for it to come to the graves first.

objectives.text: Tell Bel Axtree what to do with the other ink

options.text: Read the other ink aloud at the graves.
Send it to the Wardens' Rest.
